content.prompt: Find two possible values of $t$ that make the equation $t(10-t)=21$ true.

answer.worked:
For $t=3$:
$$\begin{align*}t(10-t)&=3(10-3)\\t(10-t)&=21\end{align*}$$
For $t=7$:
$$\begin{align*}t(10-t)&=7(10-7)\\t(10-t)&=21\end{align*}$$
Both values make the equation true.

inlines.text: Is there a limit to the number of solutions?

answer.short: For example, $(x,y)=(1,11)$, $(2,12)$ and $(-42.39,-32.39)$. There are infinitely many solutions.
answer.worked:
The example pairs satisfy the equation:
$$\begin{align*}11&=1+10\\12&=2+10\\-32.39&=-42.39+10\end{align*}$$
Any value of $x$ gives a corresponding value $y=x+10$, so there are infinitely many solution pairs.

content.prompt: These equations are equivalent. Determine the operation that has been done to both sides.

answer.worked:
Multiply both sides by $2$, including every term.
$$\begin{align*}2\times4&=2(12-x)\\8&=24-2x\end{align*}$$

Divide both sides by $4$, including every term.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{40}{4}+\frac{4b}{4}&=\frac{80}{4}\\10+b&=20\end{align*}$$

Divide both sides by $2$, including every term.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{2x}{2}+\frac{3}{2}&=\frac{5}{2}\\x+\frac{3}{2}&=\frac{5}{2}\end{align*}$$

inlines.text: Use this method of dividing first to solve the following equations, and then check that you get the same answer as if you subtracted first.

answer.worked:
Dividing first:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{2x}{2}+\frac{6}{2}&=\frac{12}{2}\\x+3&=6\\x&=3\end{align*}$$
Subtracting first:
$$\begin{align*}2x&=12-6\\2x&=6\\x&=3\end{align*}$$
Both methods give $x=3$.

Dividing first:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{4x}{4}+\frac{12}{4}&=\frac{16}{4}\\x+3&=4\\x&=1\end{align*}$$
Subtracting first:
$$\begin{align*}4x&=16-12\\4x&=4\\x&=1\end{align*}$$
Both methods give $x=1$.

Dividing first:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{10x}{10}+\frac{30}{10}&=\frac{50}{10}\\x+3&=5\\x&=2\end{align*}$$
Subtracting first:
$$\begin{align*}10x&=50-30\\10x&=20\\x&=2\end{align*}$$
Both methods give $x=2$.

Dividing first:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{2x}{2}+\frac{5}{2}&=\frac{13}{2}\\x+\frac{5}{2}&=\frac{13}{2}\\x&=\frac{13}{2}-\frac{5}{2}\\x&=4\end{align*}$$
Subtracting first:
$$\begin{align*}2x&=13-5\\2x&=8\\x&=4\end{align*}$$
Both methods give $x=4$.

Dividing first:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{5x}{5}+\frac{4}{5}&=\frac{19}{5}\\x+\frac{4}{5}&=\frac{19}{5}\\x&=\frac{19}{5}-\frac{4}{5}\\x&=3\end{align*}$$
Subtracting first:
$$\begin{align*}5x&=19-4\\5x&=15\\x&=3\end{align*}$$
Both methods give $x=3$.

Dividing first:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{3}{2}+\frac{2x}{2}&=\frac{5}{2}\\\frac{3}{2}+x&=\frac{5}{2}\\x&=\frac{5}{2}-\frac{3}{2}\\x&=1\end{align*}$$
Subtracting first:
$$\begin{align*}2x&=5-3\\2x&=2\\x&=1\end{align*}$$
Both methods give $x=1$.

Dividing first:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{8}{2}&=\frac{2x}{2}+\frac{4}{2}\\4&=x+2\\2&=x\\x&=2\end{align*}$$
Subtracting first:
$$\begin{align*}8-4&=2x\\4&=2x\\x&=2\end{align*}$$
Both methods give $x=2$.

Dividing first:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{10}{4}&=\frac{4x}{4}+\frac{10}{4}\\\frac{5}{2}&=x+\frac{5}{2}\\0&=x\\x&=0\end{align*}$$
Subtracting first:
$$\begin{align*}10-10&=4x\\0&=4x\\x&=0\end{align*}$$
Both methods give $x=0$.

content.prompt: By considering the two questions above, explain how to determine whether to expand first or divide first when solving equations with brackets.

answer.short: Dividing first is often simpler when it gives a whole number; otherwise, expanding first can avoid early fractions. Both methods are valid.
answer.worked: For $6(x-9)=24$, dividing by 6 first gives $x-9=4$, so the working uses whole numbers. For $6(x-9)=22$, dividing first gives $x-9=\frac{11}{3}$, whereas expanding first keeps whole numbers until the final division. Choose the method that makes the arithmetic easier; both give the same solution.

content.prompt: Four consecutive integers add up to 27.

answer.worked:
Let $n$ be the smallest integer. The four consecutive integers are $n$, $n+1$, $n+2$ and $n+3$.

Subtract $3m$ from both sides, then subtract $2$ and divide by $5$.
$$\begin{align*}7&=5m+2\\5&=5m\\1&=m\end{align*}$$

Subtract $4t$ from both sides, then add $6$ and divide by $3$.
$$\begin{align*}3t-6&=5\\3t&=11\\t&=\frac{11}{3}\end{align*}$$

Subtract $2h$ from both sides, then add $8$ and divide by $4$.
$$\begin{align*}4h-8&=-7\\4h&=1\\h&=\frac{1}{4}\end{align*}$$

Subtract $3w$ from both sides, then add $4$ and divide by $3$.
$$\begin{align*}12&=3w-4\\16&=3w\\\frac{16}{3}&=w\end{align*}$$

Subtract $2p$ from both sides, then divide by $3$.
$$\begin{align*}3p&=8\\p&=\frac{8}{3}\end{align*}$$

Subtract $2p$ from both sides, then divide by $3$.
$$\begin{align*}3p&=-8\\p&=-\frac{8}{3}\end{align*}$$

Subtract $k$ from both sides, then add $3$ and divide by $5$.
$$\begin{align*}-19&=5k-3\\-16&=5k\\-\frac{16}{5}&=k\end{align*}$$

Collect like terms on the right. Subtract $t$ from both sides, then divide by $5$.
$$\begin{align*}6t&=t+8\\5t&=8\\t&=\frac{8}{5}\end{align*}$$

spec.answerVisibility: Angle expressions are permanent givens; the supplied value of x is excluded from the question diagram.

answer.worked:
Vertically opposite angles are equal.
$$\begin{align*}
6x-5 &= 4x+35\\
2x-5 &= 35\\

\end{align*}$$
Both labelled angles are $115^\circ$.

spec.description: A nearly vertical straight line leaning right towards its upper endpoint crosses a diagonal rising from lower left to upper right. Four angle arcs associate the labels with their sectors.
spec.mathematics: Upper-right acute angle (2z + 7)°; lower-left acute angle (x + 10)°; upper-left obtuse angle (9x)°; lower-right obtuse angle (3y)°. Opposite angles are equal and adjacent angles sum to 180°.
spec.answerVisibility: All four algebraic angle labels are permanent givens; supplied pronumeral values are excluded from the question diagram.

answer.worked:
Adjacent angles on a straight line sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}
9x+(x+10) &= 180\\
10x+10 &= 180\\
10x &= 170\\
x &= 17
\end{align*}$$
Vertically opposite angles are equal.
$$\begin{align*}
3y &= 9(17)\\
3y &= 153\\
y &= 51
\end{align*}$$
The other pair of vertically opposite angles is equal.
$$\begin{align*}
2z+7 &= 17+10\\
2z+7 &= 27\\
2z &= 20\\
z &= 10
\end{align*}$$
The angles are $27^\circ$ and $153^\circ$, which sum to $180^\circ$.

Both labelled angles are $93^\circ$.

classification.difficultyReason: Form an equal-area equation from a composite diagram, solve it and distinguish the outside perimeter from the shared boundary.

content.prompt: Rectangles A and B have the same area.

spec.description: Unshaded stepped shape with rectangle A below-left and rectangle B above-right. Their shared horizontal boundary is dashed red and labelled x. The 15.5 dimension arrow spans B's exposed lower-right edge.
spec.mathematics: A has height 10 and width 6+x. B has height 5 and width 15.5+x. Drawing coordinates preserve the source sketch's proportions and are not a measurement scale.
spec.answerVisibility: All seven source labels are permanent givens. No supplied answer appears in the question diagram.

answer.worked:
The widths of A and B are $6+x$ and $15.5+x$. Their areas are equal.
$$\begin{align*}10(6+x)&=5(15.5+x)\\60+10x&=77.5+5x\\60+5x&=77.5\\5x&=17.5\\x&=3.5\end{align*}$$
Check:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Area of A}&=10(6+3.5)=95\\\text{Area of B}&=5(15.5+3.5)=95\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: State the perimeter of the shape.

answer.worked:
$6+3.5=9.5$ and $15.5+3.5=19$. Add both rectangle perimeters and subtract the shared edge twice, since it is internal.
$$\begin{align*}P&=2(9.5+10)+2(19+5)-2(3.5)\\&=39+48-7\\&=80\end{align*}$$
